steps.tx: A rare, severe extra-articular manifestation of long-standing seropositive rheumatoid arthritis combines chronic deforming arthritis with haematological abnormalities. Diagnosing **felty syndrome** requires the classical clinical triad of severe deforming rheumatoid arthritis, prominent splenomegaly, and absolute neutropenia (absolute neutrophil count under 1,500 per microlitre). Patients harbour high titres of rheumatoid factor and anti-CCP antibodies, extensive subcutaneous rheumatoid nodules, and an elevated risk of recurrent life-threatening bacterial skin and pulmonary infections. Splenic sequestration and anti-neutrophil autoantibodies drive the profound peripheral neutropenia.
steps.say: A rare extra-articular manifestation of long-standing seropositive rheumatoid arthritis combines chronic deforming arthritis with haematological abnormalities. Diagnosing felty syndrome requires the classical clinical triad of severe rheumatoid arthritis, prominent splenomegaly, and absolute neutropenia. Patients harbour high titres of rheumatoid factor, extensive subcutaneous nodules, and elevated risks of recurrent bacterial infections. Splenic sequestration and autoantibodies drive the profound neutropenia.

rows: High titres of RF and anti-CCP
Clonal CD3+ CD8+ CD57+ T-cell expansion
Occurs in up to 30% of Felty cases

steps.tx: The unique combination of rheumatoid arthritis with occupational coal workers pneumoconiosis produces multiple rapidly developing necrotizing pulmonary nodules. Designated as **caplan syndrome** (rheumatoid pneumoconiosis), coal dust, silica, or asbestos inhalation triggers an exaggerated immune reaction in patients with underlying rheumatoid genetic susceptibility. Chest radiography reveals bilateral, rounded, well-circumscribed peripheral lung nodules measuring one to five centimetres, which can cavitate, calcify, or trigger spontaneous pneumothorax. Histopathologically, Caplan nodules display central necrotic debris mixed with black coal dust pigment surrounded by a characteristic palisading fibroblast border.
steps.say: The unique combination of rheumatoid arthritis with occupational coal workers pneumoconiosis produces multiple rapidly developing pulmonary nodules. Designated as caplan syndrome, coal dust or silica inhalation triggers an exaggerated immune reaction in patients with rheumatoid susceptibility. Chest radiography reveals bilateral peripheral lung nodules that can cavitate or calcify. Histopathologically, Caplan nodules display central necrotic debris mixed with coal dust surrounded by palisading fibroblasts.

left.title: Caplan Syndrome Nodules
points: Coal dust / silica exposure + Seropositive RA
Rapid appearance of multiple bilateral lung nodules
Nodules measure 1 to 5 cm in lung periphery
Histology: Central necrosis with black coal rings
May cavitate and produce mild hemoptysis

right.title: Simple Rheumatoid Lung Nodules
points: Occurs in seropositive RA without dust exposure
Subpleural asymptomatic peripheral nodules
Histology identical to subcutaneous nodules
Typically stable in size and non-cavitary
Requires biopsy if solitary to exclude malignancy

steps.tx: First-line conventional synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic therapy utilizes folate antagonism to suppress autoimmune synovial proliferation. Prescribing **methotrexate** (MTX) weekly induces intracellular polyglutamylation, inhibiting aminoimidazolecarboxamide ribonucleotide (AICAR) transformylase and thymidylate synthase. This drives extracellular adenosine accumulation, suppressing pro-inflammatory cytokine secretion while inducing lymphocyte apoptosis. Crucially, oral folic acid (one to five milligrams daily, omitted on MTX day) must be co-prescribed to prevent stomatitis, gastrointestinal upset, and cytopenias. Regular monitoring of complete blood counts and liver enzymes is mandatory; methotrexate is strictly teratogenic.
steps.say: First-line conventional synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic therapy utilizes folate antagonism to suppress autoimmune synovial proliferation. Prescribing methotrexate weekly induces intracellular polyglutamylation, driving extracellular adenosine accumulation that suppresses pro-inflammatory cytokines. Co-prescribing folic acid prevents stomatitis, nausea, and cytopenias. Regular monitoring of complete blood counts and liver enzymes is mandatory, and methotrexate is strictly contraindicated in pregnancy.

steps.tx: An oral synthetic antimalarial agent serves as an essential, well-tolerated component of combination DMARD therapy in mild or early disease. Prescribing **hydroxychloroquine** accumulates in intracellular lysosomes, raising intralysosomal pH and impairing antigen presentation on MHC class II molecules to T cells. Hydroxychloroquine provides excellent joint control without inducing myelosuppression, renal toxicity, or hepatic injury, rendering it exceptionally safe in pregnancy. However, long-term accumulation in retinal pigment epithelial cells risks irreversible bull's-eye maculopathy, mandating baseline and annual automated visual field testing and optical coherence tomography after five years.

Hydroxychloroquine provides joint control without myelosuppression or liver toxicity, rendering it safe in pregnancy. Long-term retinal accumulation risks irreversible maculopathy, requiring annual visual field testing after five years of therapy.

rows: Increases lysosomal pH / Impairs MHC II
2 to 3 grams orally daily in divided doses

steps.tx: A synthetic isoxazole derivative inhibits de novo pyrimidine synthesis to arrest the proliferation of activated autoimmune lymphocytes. Prescribing **leflunomide** rapidly converts in the gut wall and liver to its active metabolite teriflunomide, which non-competitively inhibits dihydroorotate dehydrogenase (DHODH) in the inner mitochondrial membrane. Because proliferating T and B lymphocytes lack salvage pathways and depend entirely on de novo pyrimidine synthesis, leflunomide selectively halts their G1-to-S cell cycle transition. Adverse effects include hepatotoxicity, hypertension, diarrhoea, and teratogenicity, requiring accelerated cholestyramine washout before planned conception.

nodes.label: Rapid Conversion to Active Metabolite Teriflunomide (A77 1726)
Non-Competitive Inhibition of Mitochondrial DHODH Enzyme
Depletes UMP Pools: Halts Lymphocyte G1/S Proliferation

steps.tx: Biologic disease-modifying agents neutralizing tumour necrosis factor revolutionized the management of refractory inflammatory polyarthritis. Prescribing **tnf inhibitors** includes monoclonal antibodies (infliximab, adalimumab, golimumab), pegylated Fab fragments (certolizumab pegol), and circulating soluble receptor decoys (etanercept). Neutralizing soluble and transmembrane TNF-alpha rapidly suppresses synovial chemokine expression, endothelial leukocyte adhesion, and osteoclast activation, halting radiographic joint erosions. Crucially, because TNF maintains granuloma integrity, all patients must undergo screening for latent tuberculosis (tuberculin skin test or interferon-gamma release assay) and hepatitis B prior to initiating therapy.
steps.say: Biologic disease-modifying agents neutralizing tumour necrosis factor revolutionized the management of refractory inflammatory polyarthritis. Prescribing TNF inhibitors includes monoclonal antibodies such as adalimumab and soluble receptor decoys like etanercept. Neutralizing TNF rapidly suppresses synovial inflammation and halts radiographic joint erosions. Because TNF maintains granuloma integrity, all patients must undergo screening for latent tuberculosis and hepatitis B prior to initiating therapy.

steps.tx: Oral targeted synthetic small molecules directly block intracellular Janus kinase signaling downstream of multiple cytokine receptors. Administering **tofacitinib** or baricitinib competitively inhibits the ATP-binding pocket of JAK1 and JAK3 (and JAK2), preventing phosphorylation of STAT transcription factors involved in interleukin-2, IL-6, and interferon signaling. Taken orally without cold-chain storage requirements, JAK inhibitors provide rapid relief of pain and synovitis comparable to biologic agents. Adverse considerations include dose-dependent herpes zoster reactivation (mandating recombinant zoster vaccination), venous thromboembolism, and major adverse cardiovascular events in high-risk patients.
steps.say: Oral targeted synthetic small molecules directly block intracellular Janus kinase signaling downstream of multiple cytokine receptors. Administering tofacitinib competitively inhibits the ATP-binding pocket of JAK enzymes, preventing phosphorylation of STAT transcription factors. Taken orally without cold-chain requirements, JAK inhibitors provide rapid relief of synovitis. Adverse considerations include herpes zoster reactivation, requiring recombinant vaccination, and increased venous thromboembolism risk in predisposed patients.

left.title: Targeted Synthetic JAK Inhibitors (Tofacitinib)
points: Oral once or twice-daily dosing
Intracellular inhibition of JAK1/JAK3 enzymes
Rapid onset of clinical analgesia within days
Recombinant Shingrix zoster vaccine mandatory
Black box: VTE, MACE, and malignancy risk

right.title: Biologic DMARDs (Anti-TNF / Anti-IL6)
points: Subcutaneous or IV infusion protocols
Extracellular cytokine neutralization
Requires cold-chain refrigeration transport
Latent TB screening mandatory prior to start
Risk of demyelinating disease and heart failure

steps.tx: Managing active cytopenias and recurrent infections in Felty syndrome requires disease-modifying immunosuppression paired with colony-stimulating factor support. Frontline therapy for Felty syndrome utilizes oral **methotrexate** (15 to 25 milligrams weekly), which paradoxically improves peripheral neutrophil counts while controlling articular disease activity. In patients presenting with severe, life-threatening neutropenia (ANC < 500 per microlitre) complicated by active bacterial sepsis, subcutaneous granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF) accelerates myeloid recovery. Refractory cases unresponsive to DMARDs or rituximab achieve haematological remission following elective surgical splenectomy.

nodes.label: Documented Felty Syndrome: RA + Splenomegaly + Neutropenia
Severe Infection / ANC < 500: Add Subcutaneous G-CSF
Refractory Cytopenias: Rituximab or Elective Splenectomy
